title: Incremental redaction staging airlock for console metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Console telemetry (route-level metrics, feature-flag events, developer API traces) contains fields that may include customer-identifying values. Current pipeline hard-deletes or attempts full-field scrubbing in batch backfills which is opaque and high-risk for analytics regressions. We need an incremental, observable staging path (an 'airlock') that lets privacy engineers and SREs preview, test, and approve redaction transforms before they are promoted to the canonical analytics store.

Scope: Build a staging airlock layer between the ingest bus and the main analytics warehouse for console metrics. Capabilities: 1) replayable quarantine store that preserves raw payloads for short window (configurable, default 7 days) with strict KMS encryption and access audit; 2) transformation manifest system (versioned redaction/transforms) that can be applied in dry-run mode to generate preview diffs; 3) preview API and query canary that allows product/insights to assert invariants (row counts, histogram deltas) before commit; 4) safe promote path that atomically swaps a redacted partition into the main analytics view with tombstone propagation to downstream aggregates; 5) incremental backfill worker to apply transforms to historical partitions with rate limiting and failure scavenging; 6) attestation log for compliance showing who approved which manifest and commit.

Design constraints: airlock must not increase critical-path latency for live dashboards (redaction runs async); must support schema evolution (transform manifests tied to schema versions); transformations are deterministic and idempotent; previews produce signed diffs for audit; retain raw data only for short windows with automatic crypto-shred.

Technical approach: implement a new microservice (analytics-airlock) that subscribes to the internal ingest Kafka topic and writes to an encrypted S3 quarantine prefix (partitioned by day). Manifests are stored in the Config Service (git-style versioning) and executed by a separate transform worker using our existing sanitization library. Preview API (/admin/analytics/redact-preview) takes manifest id + query window and returns summary diffs and sample redacted rows (redacted samples are k-anonymized before display). Promote path writes redacted partitions to the analytics warehouse and emits a commit event consumed by downstream materializers. Backfill orchestrator uses Job Runner with checkpointed progress and canary checkpoints.

Rollout plan: start with console metrics namespace only (non-customer-identifying events) in dry-run for 2 weeks, then enable preview for privacy/PM, then small promote canary on one compute region for 48 hours, monitor, then full promote. Backfill historical 30 days in low-traffic windows after promote.

Operational concerns: audit-tail must be queryable for compliance requests; ensure RBAC around preview API and quarantine S3; telemetry for staging vs promoted views; cost estimates for short-term raw retention.

Success metric: ability to stage and promote redaction manifests with zero undetected analytic regressions in canary, and the ability to generate attestation reports for audits in < 1 hour.
acceptance_criteria: Airlock service ingests console telemetry and writes encrypted quarantine partitions (7d retention) to S3
Manifest authoring UI + API (versioned) that accepts transform rules and stores manifest metadata with approver identity
Preview API returns deterministic diffs and redacted sample rows (k-anonymized) and enforces RBAC
Promote flow atomically swaps redacted partitions into the analytics warehouse and emits commit events
Backfill orchestrator can process historical partitions with checkpointing and resume after failures
Attestation log contains signed entries for preview approvals and promote commits, exportable as CSV/JSON for compliance
Integration tests + end-to-end canary show no more than 1% delta in non-PII metrics after dry-run validation
Security review completed and SRE runbook for incident / rollback created
comments: 2026-02-16 — Kickoff: scoped to console metrics only.  Agreed quarantine retention 7 days by default; product asked for 14-day option for edge cases.
2026-02-22 — Architecture review: decided on async redaction to avoid dashboard latency regressions. Marco to prototype transform worker using existing sanitizer library (ENG-83421 reference).

2026-03-01 — Prototype complete: analytics-airlock writes to s3://redwood-quarantine/console/YYYY-MM-DD. Small perf regression observed in consumer lag under burst; added rate limiter on writer. See PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1532
2026-03-04 — Security notes: quarantine prefix must be KMS-encrypted with access only via the airlock role; audit exports only via attestation log. Security review kickoff: @Sophie Grant assigned.
2026-03-07 — QA: preview API returning diffs for sample query window. Privacy team requested redact-sample masking to remove trailing context (implemented).

2026-03-09 — Code review feedback: add deterministic hashing for id replacement, ensure transforms are idempotent. Updated transform manifest schema accordingly. PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-airlock/pull/47
2026-03-10 — Scheduled: security review in-progress; integration test harness for canary has been wired to staging dashboards (grafana board: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/analytics-airlock).
